content.comment_body: Hello, are there any examples demonstrating the use of NC or NO contacts in the [product_name] configuration tool? For instance, if Relay1 is activated, is there a way to prevent Relay2 from activating by placing a NC contact in series with the Relay2 coil? That’s the kind of scenario I’m interested in. Thanks!
Hi, you can find many examples at [url]. There’s even a case with interlocked outputs available there. Regards,

Thanks [user_name], I’m finding this quite challenging! Your diagram helped me understand two things I hadn’t seen before: how to invert inputs on function blocks, and how to build in ladder format and convert it with the special button to view the logic as a function block diagram. I feel ready to continue now. Thanks!

Glad I could help. I’d like to mention something important: always select the correct hardware before starting your programming. Otherwise, you might develop a solution that isn’t compatible with your hardware type. If you choose the hardware first in the tool, then only the functions supported by your device will be available for selection. There’s an illustrative image about this. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: A user asked for examples on how to configure NO/NC contacts in [product_name] programming software, especially for relay interlocking scenarios. The main challenge was finding clear guidance on basic logic and tool features like input inversion and diagram conversions. With help from the community, the user quickly learned those features and continued their project.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for clear, accessible examples and simple methods to configure NO/NC contacts and create interlock logic in the [product_name] software, along with better ways to discover relevant features.
